decisions.title: Too busy to be tired
decisions.situation: Laura says it is time for a nap. You have been awake for ages and have only inspected half the room.

choices.label: Give your eyes a short test closure
Ask Laura to stay for a minute
Explain your position at full volume

result.title: Test extended
result.body: You wake up later. The uninspected half of the room is still there.

journal.text: I fell asleep while checking whether I needed a nap.

decisions.title: Encore! Encore!
decisions.situation: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

choices.label: Give the full concert
Try a different rhythm
Look inside the bowl

result.title: A short, loud career
result.body: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

journal.text: I discovered how much noise a spoon and a bowl could make.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Laura asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Show Laura your disappearing treasure
Try the other sock
Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Laura supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Laura the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: Unlimited dragons, limited shelf space
decisions.situation: At the library, you find a book so big you need both arms to carry it. The return desk suddenly looks very far away.

choices.label: Commit to the enormous book
Find a smaller story you love
Ask the librarian for a recommendation

result.title: An ambitious loan
result.body: You finish some of it, skip a confusing chapter, and learn three words you immediately misuse.

journal.text: I borrowed the largest book I could carry.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: The staffroom boss fight
decisions.situation: You copied your school map from a video game. Gabriel wants to know why the staffroom is labelled “FINAL BOSS” and the toilets contain treasure.

choices.label: Replace the monsters with actual rooms
Ask whether the staffroom really is off limits
Insist the treasure is in the toilets

result.title: A less dangerous school
result.body: You redraw the map. The dragon becomes the library. Gabriel marks the corrected version and circles the one staircase you accidentally kept.

journal.text: I replaced a video-game map with a real map of my school.

decisions.title: They do not find it funny
decisions.situation: Someone keeps making a joke out of Gabriel’s name. Gabriel has stopped correcting them.

choices.label: Use their name properly and speak up
Check on Gabriel privately
Join in for a laugh

result.title: A little backup
result.body: You say it is getting old. Gabriel thanks you later.

journal.text: I backed Gabriel when someone kept mocking their name.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Laura’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Tell Laura what happened
Offer to help repair it
Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Laura is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Laura’s mug.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Gabriel whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them
Help make a short apology
Add microwave sound effects

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Gabriel said anything worse.

decisions.title: Fastest toy car alive
decisions.situation: You invented the numbers for a marked science report. Your toy car apparently reached 90,000 kilometres an hour. Alice asks to see the original measurements.

choices.label: Admit it and take the report back
Offer a live demonstration instead
Invent a second sheet of measurements

result.title: The car has been recalled
result.body: Alice lets you submit a properly measured replacement with a reduced mark. The real car rolls under a cupboard. You record that too.

journal.text: I admitted inventing science data and replaced my report with real measurements.

decisions.title: Selective honesty
decisions.situation: Alice has marked a correct answer wrong and a wrong answer right. The mistakes cancel out. You could mention both, or suddenly become very interested in only one.

choices.label: Point out both mistakes
Get the answers explained properly
Ask for the lost marks. Hide the free ones.

result.title: No profit, better reputation
result.body: Alice corrects both marks and thanks you for being honest. Your grade stays exactly where it was.

journal.text: I showed Alice two marking mistakes that cancelled each other out.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in São Paulo takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in São Paulo needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in São Paulo.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Congratulations, almost
decisions.situation: A caller says you have won a fortune in a lottery you never entered. To release the prize, they need a “small verification payment”. They sound personally hurt that you have questions.

choices.label: End the call before sharing anything
Ask how they feel about their life choices
Dictate a completely invented forty-letter name

result.title: Your fortune remains imaginary
result.body: You hang up. The only thing you lose is the chance to hear which payment methods the imaginary lottery prefers.

journal.text: I ended a suspicious lottery call without sending money.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Laura also confessed to approving the haircut.

Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in São Paulo.

decisions.title: You need medical attention

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer
